institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the university and the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I believe that it was very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any assistance. I received a lot of emails from the hosting university in advance so that it was easy for me to know what to do when I arrived in my study destination.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was satisfied with this. Lots of information were available. However, it was hard to get in contact with the administration regarding specific questions, as the opening time slots were small, and many students had questions for the administration.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found mine via a Facebook Group called "Padam Padam" - a Danish-Paris groups where people write if they rent out their apartments in Paris.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be quite hard to find a place to live, plus it might be more expensive than back in Copenhagen. So, save up some money prior the your exchange trip.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think I saw somewhere that the hosting university afforded some help for housing, but I did not discover this further as I found something on my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was very stressfull. On a specific timeslot in a day in July, all students at the host institution should register at the same time for the same courses online, first come, first served. If you were too late to register for a course, than just bad luck for you. Lucky for me, I got all the mandatory courses that I needed, but this was not the case for some of my fellow students. They simply were too slow (I believe it was a matter of seconds when trying to register online) to get the needed and mandatory courses, and thus they ended up missing some of these courses, as the administration could not move then around later on. I believe this is problematic when some students are going on exchange with mandatory course to take, and that they can not be sure whether they will be granted to have the courses after being granted an exchange semester at the host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I believe that too little help was available right after the registration process. It was hard to get in contact with the administration in case of specific questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up registering for the classes I needed, but some of my fellow students did not get the courses they needed in order to get merit from UCPH - due to the registration process of "first come, first served".

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: to make sure that your wifi connection is stable so that you can register for the courses as fast as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I was satisfied. the life at sciences po is rather different that what I am used to at UCPH. The courses are much more practical and empirical oriented that they are at the BA-level at UCPH - which was nice. However, looking solely at the teachings, the level was way lower than UCPH, as the teachings were far less pedagogical as also mentioned below. Overall, I was still satisfied, and it was nice to experience another approach to being a student at a university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, I believe that the level of the courses were lower than what I'm used to from back at my sending university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Far less pedagogical and more hierarcichal at Sciences Po compared to UCPH. However, the classes were more cased based and more practical and empirical oriented, which I liked a lot. Also, most of the courses consisted of 5 ECTS and were solely class-based with no lectures. This created more room for two-way communication between teacher and students, and it also created greater room for discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
DAFF 25A36 - From Ajax Operation to the Nuclear Deal: an introduction to contemporary Iran
DAFF 25A99 - Small and Micro-states in Global Politics
DSPO 25A02 – European Integration and its Challenges: The Euro, Migration and Populism
DAFF 25A71 – European Political Economy
ASPO 25A11 - Comparative Politics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly recommend the following four courses:

(1) DAFF 25A36 - From Ajax Operation to the Nuclear Deal: an introduction to contemporary Iran
(2) DAFF 25A99 - Small and Micro-states in Global Politics
(3) DSPO 25A02 – European Integration and its Challenges: The Euro, Migration and Populism
(4) DAFF 25A71 – European Political Economy.

They were all very oriented and included interesting cases during the classes. Especially the course on European Political Economy was very instructive and interesting to follow, with good teaching as well.

The fifth course, I took (ASPO 25A11 - Comparative Politics), was not as well executed as the other courses. I missed a red threat between the syllabus, the class-teachings, and the lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the general cost of living in Paris are high, but they also differ a lot depending on where you are in the city. A cup of coffee or a lunch might be much cheaper in areas that are not located around the Seine.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Paris is in general an expensive city. However, what was less expensive than what I expected, was the lunch program called Crous. Here, you get very cheap lunch served in big portions. Great value for money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were lots of activities and opportunities, but I did not discover many of them. I participated at some of the BDE (student organisation) - organized parties.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many things, especially through the BDE (student services). I did not engage in any of these student activities, but I attended a yoga course through Sciences Po, which I liked. Many other sport forms were also available, such as tennis, football, MMA, running, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated the hatha yoga-class, which I can highly recommend. These classes were a good way to stress off and experience something else.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
discover the outher arrondissements of Paris, especially 10e arr and
Belleville.Also
, I can recommend  to take a weekend trip to Marseille if possible (the French train system is amazing) - especially when the weather is still good - I went there late september, and it was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me, it was easy. I went to Paris with some of my best friends from back in Copenhagen, so it was easy and comfortable to land in a new city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open. Initiative is warmly welcomed. Everyone is kind of nervous and overwhelmed in the beginning of the semester, and therefore it was nice when people opened up and initiated conversations themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the most challenging would be that people come from all over the world, but this would also be the most interesting part. to get to know people from other parts of the world

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the way that it was more laid-back compared to at home. As a student at the university there are always more pages to read, more work that could have been done, but I believe that the "culture" (if one cal call it that) was a little more laid-back, which I appreciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) lots of school assignments. It is an elite university, which is easy to feel with all the presentations and papers to write during the semester.
2) the level of the education is generally a bit lower than what I am used to from back in UCPH.
3) the empirical approach of Sciences Po is very interesting, kind of refreshing in contrast to the rather theoretically driven UCPH bachelor

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: attend and engage in the class seminars. Easy points in the bag if you overcome the burden of speaking another language and engage in the discussions during the sessions. Also, participating actively makes the sessions more interesting.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience the city of Paris and another academic environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: to overcome the hurdle of speaking academic English, but I also learned a lot from this in the end. So, I will highly recommend to just do it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
